newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. envoy Ross threatens to leave Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. envoy Ross threatens to leave Hebron talks.

text.p: U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross is threatening to leave the Middle East on Monday unless dramatic progress is made in Israeli-PLO talks on carrying out a Hebron redeployment, PLO and diplomatic sources said.

PLO negotiator Hassan Asfour said Ross, who arrived 15 days ago, told Palestinian President Yasser Arafat he planned to leave on Monday. A diplomatic source, asked about Asfour's comment, said: "It's a good possibility".
"Ross informed Arafat and the Palestinians on Saturday night that if there was no progress on Sunday night he planned to leave for Washington. He had other things to work on," Asfour told Reuters.

The PLO official said Washington would continue to be represented in the talks by U.S. Ambassador to Israel Martin Indyk and U.S. Consul General in East Jerusalem Edward Abington. Ross scheduled a news conference for 1400 GMT on Monday.

The diplomatic source, who declined to be identified, said: "If things cannot be done immediately he (Ross) would come back when the parties get closer...There aren't that many things left which have to be resolved. It's a matter of hammering the language out on paper."

Israel was supposed to pull back from Hebron in March under a peace deal with the PLO but delayed the withdrawal because of Islamic suicide attacks that killed 59 people and demands by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to bolster security for 400 Jews living and studying in enclaves among the 100,000 Arabs of Hebron.
